caption: What if a spoonful of neutron star hit Earth? When a giant star dies in a supernova, its core is crushed into a neutron star: roughly the mass of our Sun packed into a ball about 20 km wide. NASA says a single sugar cube of that material would weigh about 1 billion tonnes on Earth, more than all 8 billion humans put together (roughly 390 million tonnes). The fastest known neutron star spins more than 700 times a second, over 100 times faster than a ceiling fan on full speed. Bring a spoonful here and, freed from the star's crushing gravity, it would burst in a giant explosion. The twist: scientists think much of Earth's gold may have been forged when neutron stars collided, so that Dhanteras gold coin might be colliding-star stuff. Would YOU hold a spoonful? 👇
